### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-odata`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **60** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-odata/README.md`, `packages/drivers/driver-odata/package.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/datasource.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-odata/README.md`, `packages/drivers/driver-odata/package.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/datasource.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **21** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `41d718d8f47207b2c9daef83a94745df0dcba382` — the merge of head `3351ae356419278f5c8ced5c10eccb2ff057f844` into base `d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 41d718d8f47207b2c9daef83a94745df0dcba382 && git checkout 41d718d8f47207b2c9daef83a94745df0dcba382
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2 3351ae356419278f5c8ced5c10eccb2ff057f844 && git checkout -B drift-repro d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2 && git merge --no-ff 3351ae356419278f5c8ced5c10eccb2ff057f844

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Advisory runs skipped as expected (dogfood matrix, opt-in harnesses). Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.

**A. New published seam in `@objectstack/types` (`packages/types/src/connector-credential-source.ts`, re-exported from `index.ts`).** `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_SERVICE` (`'connector-credential-source'`), `BorrowedConnectorAuth` (bearer / api-key with `headerName` and optional `paramName` / basic), `BorrowedConnectorCredential` (`auth`, optional `expiresAt`), `ConnectorCredentialRequest` (`organizationId`), `ConnectorCredentialHandle` (`connector`, `get`, `refresh`), `IConnectorCredentialSource` (`borrow`), `connectorCredentialRefusal`, `BORROWED_CREDENTIAL_SKEW_MS`, `BorrowedCredentialCallOptions`, `callWithBorrowedCredential`. **Right** as a seam: the module imports nothing, so the dependency direction the D7 ruling left open is answered without a new edge (service-automation, service-datasource and driver-odata each already depend on, or now depend on, `@objectstack/types`; `objectql` untouched). The three auth shapes map one-to-one onto `ConnectorInstanceBearerAuthSchema` / `ConnectorInstanceAPIKeyAuthSchema` (`headerName`, `paramName`) / `ConnectorInstanceBasicAuthSchema` (`username`) in `packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts`, read at the head; the lender's `borrowedAuthOf` switch is exhaustive over `ConnectorInstanceAuth` minus `none`.

**B. The call helper's rule.** `callWithBorrowedCredential`: `get`, refresh when `expiresAt` minus the skew margin is at or before `now()`, send, on a 401 (result predicate defaulting to `status === 401`, or a throw declaring `status`/`statusCode` 401) refresh once and send again, a second 401 throws `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` naming the instance with a fixed sentence; every other result returns and every other throw propagates, handle refusals included. **Right** against the card's wording (refresh on expiry, once on 401, then the floor's 503) and against the plugin-driver floor read at `packages/objectql/src/external-driver-floor.ts`: a thrown error with `status` 503 is outside `EXTERNAL_READ_REFUSED_STATUSES` {400, 404, 422} and `EXTERNAL_WRITE_REFUSED_STATUSES`, so the floor answers `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` with the message in the server log only. 12 unit cases pin each branch, including single flight and the handle-refusal pass-through.

**C. The lender (`service-automation/src/connector-credential-source.ts`, registered in `init()` and added to `providesServices`).** `borrow` judges the declaration read by `readDeclaredConnectorItems(ctx, { post: true })` (signature verified at the head: returns `unknown[] | undefined`, throws on an unreadable declaration) and refuses 422 for undeclared / no `provider` / no `auth` or `type: 'none'` / `enabled: false`, 503 when unreadable. A handle resolves `auth.credentialRef` through `connectorCredentialChain(ctx)` (env, then one `store.read(ref)` row, then the vault; no store under a walled posture) via the existing `resolveConnectorCredential`; `missing` is 503 with `missingCredentialReason`'s remedy, `unavailable` carries the store's own fixed sentences (verified: `ConnectorCredentialStore.resolve` never interpolates the engine's message), a thrown host resolver is replaced by a fixed sentence. The held value is re-resolved when `credentialGeneration` moves, which `reconcileDeclaredConnectors` bumps on entry, and every credential door write runs a reconcile (verified at `setConnectorCredential` / `clearConnectorCredential`). **Right**, with one correction to the module docblock's claim "or the instance's declaration changing under it": a declaration change is only seen when a reconcile runs (generation) or on `refresh()`; the handle does not watch the declaration itself. Not a defect, since the reconcile is what every declaration path runs, but the docblock overstates it. 15 cases including the real store over SQLite, the five 422 refusals, the post-borrow undeclared case (503 on `get`), the host-resolver message withheld.

**D. The borrower (`service-datasource`).** `DatasourceConnectionSpec.credential?: ConnectorCredentialHandle` (public type widening on the factory contract, additive); `DatasourceConnectionServiceConfig.connectorCredentials?`; `ConnectableDatasource.external.connector?`; `DatasourceAdminServiceConfig.connectorRefusal?`; the new module `datasource-connector-credential.ts` (`borrowedConnectorOf`, `borrowConnectorCredential`, never throws). In `attemptConnect` the borrow sits after the `credentialsRef` block, before the build, answering `failed-credentials` through `handleFailure` (state `failed`, engine marked unavailable, fail-fast when objects bind, verified against `handleFailure` at the head). The admin door refuses `createDatasource` before any write, `updateDatasource` when the patch touches `external`, and `testConnection` without probing; the plugin's `probe` passes the handle to the factory. All **right as written**, and 14 cases pin them with a factory-built driver double.

**E. The first presenter (`driver-odata`).** `plugin.ts` adds a lazy `borrowed()` beside `credential()`: refuses both channels, refuses `auth.scheme !== 'none'` beside a connector, resolves the source per request through `ctx.getService`, borrows once per connector name, does not keep a refused borrow, rethrows a lend refusal without its 422 (so the floor answers 503). `transport.ts` sends through `callWithBorrowedCredential` when a handle exists, presenting bearer / basic / api-key header / api-key query parameter, the 401 body cancelled unread; the `credentialsRef` path is unchanged, including resolve-again-on-401. `odata-driver.ts` threads `borrowed` to the transport. `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` add the `@objectstack/types` workspace dependency. 11 new cases. The presentation and refusals are **right**; two things it implies are **wrong**, below.

**F. The connect-time refusal does not reach the one shipped consumer (must-fix).** The OData plugin registers its driver as a `driver.`-prefixed kernel service in `init()` ("the engine adopts `driver.*` services once every plugin has initialised", `plugin.ts` line 177 to 179); the ObjectQL plugin's `start()` discovery loop `registerDriver`s every `driver.*` service (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` line 1153); `ODataDriver.connect()` is a no-op. When the app plugin's `start()` then calls `connectDeclared`, `attemptConnect` returns `{ status: 'already-registered' }` at its first guard (`engine.getDriverByName(name)`), before the `credentialsRef` block and before the new borrow block; had the order been reversed, `factory.supports(record.driver)` is false for a plugin driver id (`createDefaultDatasourceDriverFactory.supports` is `resolveKind(driverId) !== undefined`) and `skipped-unsupported` returns before the borrow block too. So for a datasource served by `driver-odata`, which the spec makes the only accepted shape for `external.connector` (built-in database drivers and managed datasources are refused at parse), nothing judges the instance at connect: an undeclared, descriptor-only, credential-less or disabled instance boots as a registered datasource, `Setup → Datasources` shows no failure, bound objects do not fail the boot, and every read answers `503 ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` with the reason in the server log only. The admin door is not a substitute (it refuses a plugin driver id as unsupported at `datasource-admin-plugin.ts` line 872, so no runtime-origin OData datasource exists). This contradicts the card's acceptance item "an undeclared instance refused ... at connect", the PR body's "连接 fail-closed 拒绝" and "a datasource that objects bind to fails the boot", the liveness row's first anchor (`attemptConnect`, which no shipped composition reaches with a connector-naming record), and the carried flag from 6511230689 (a disabled instance surfacing visibly rather than as a silent per-read failure). The reachable branch is pinned only by a factory-built double. Fix at the borrower, where the PR says the gate is: in `attemptConnect`, judge `borrowedConnectorOf(record.external)` for an already-registered driver too (a borrow judges the declaration and resolves nothing, so this is a verdict, not a build), recording `failed-credentials` and evicting or marking the registered driver unavailable, and pin it with a test whose driver is adopted through a `driver.`-prefixed service rather than built by the factory. Alternatively the OData plugin may borrow at `start()` (the lender registers in `init()`, so init-all-then-start-all guarantees it) and fail the boot or warn loudly naming the remedy, but then the liveness evidence and the PR body must stop naming `attemptConnect` as the OData path's gate.

**G. A query-parameter API key can reach a caller-facing error body (must-fix, judged in ③, named here because it is a property of the new presenting surface).**

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/27746-datasource-borrows-connector-credential.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/types`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/driver-odata`, carrying `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching the two line-initial declarations in the PR body. What the diff publishes: new exports in `@objectstack/types`; additive optional fields on `DatasourceConnectionSpec`, `DatasourceConnectionServiceConfig`, `ConnectableDatasource.external`, `DatasourceAdminServiceConfig` in `service-datasource`; a new kernel service and a `providesServices` entry in `service-automation`; a new runtime dependency and new behaviour in `driver-odata`. No authorable key, value or type changes (the spec half landed in #27783; this PR edits `packages/spec/liveness/**` only, which is a ledger, not a schema), so `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right kind, and under the Post-Task Checklist rule the kind alone decides the level: `none` takes `patch`. The four packages named are exactly the four whose published surface moves (`packages/spec` is touched only in its liveness ledger and generated state-count, which ship no API change). The changeset body carries no model identifier. **Right.**

`Clause-②:` yes — this PR declares a widening of the runtime contract (a new seam and a new credential channel for datasources), neither `(narrowing)` nor `skip-changeset`; the declaration face is the owed review and this record is it.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Can a credential value reach a log, an error body or a stored row?** Traced from every point a value exists: the lender's `resolve` (`resolution.value`, held in the handle's closure only), `get` / `refresh` returns, `callWithBorrowedCredential`'s `credential.auth`, `presentBorrowed` in the transport.

- Logs: the lender logs nothing; `callWithBorrowedCredential` logs nothing; the transport's thrown messages use `req.subject`, never the URL or a header (the fetch-failure catch and `ODataRequestError` both, verified at the head); the connection service logs `borrow.reason`, which is the lender's refusal text naming instance and reference only; the floor logs `error.message` of a driver throw, which for the helper's 503 is the fixed sentence. **No value reaches a log from this code.**
- Stored rows: the admin door stores `external.connector` (a name); the handle is never serialized; the datasource path does not call `markRejected`. **None.**
- Error bodies: the helper's 503 and every lender refusal are fixed sentences; the 401 body is cancelled unread. **One path remains open (must-fix).** With `auth: { type: 'api-key', paramName }` the key travels in the request URL (`url.searchParams.set`). On a non-401 refusal the transport builds `ODataRequestError` from the dialect's `readError(body).message`, the upstream's own text, and for 400 / 404 / 422 the floor passes that message to the caller as `ExternalReadRefusedError` (400 `INVALID_QUERY`) whenever the `where` is attested as the caller's own, and to the server log otherwise. An upstream that echoes the request URI in its error message, which gateways and OData services commonly do for an unknown segment, therefore carries the key into a 400 error body shown to an end user. The lender's own call path anticipates exactly this (`credentialForms` in `connector-credentials.ts` lists "URL-encoded, as an api-key sent as a query parameter travels in the request URL", and `withoutCredential` / `upstreamRefusalMessage` scrub against it); the datasource presenter does not, and cannot import it. Fix: scrub the upstream message against the presented credential's spellings before building `ODataRequestError` in `transport.request` (a small helper beside `callWithBorrowedCredential` in `@objectstack/types`, so every presenter shares one rule), or refuse the `paramName` presentation for a borrowed credential until it is scrubbed; pin it with an upstream double that echoes the URL on a 404. The header forms (bearer, basic, api-key header) are not echoed by this path and are not affected.

**What happens for a disabled or missing instance.** At the lender: `borrow` refuses 422 (`VALIDATION_ERROR`) with a sentence naming the instance and the fix; an instance disabled or undeclared after the borrow is refused 503 on the next fill (generation move or `refresh`). At the admin door: create / external-touching update / test connection refused with the reason, nothing written or probed. At a factory-built driver's connect: `failed-credentials`, state `failed`, engine marked unavailable, boot fails when objects bind (pinned). At the OData driver: refused per request before anything is sent, rethrown without the 422 so the floor answers `503 ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` with the reason in the server log only, the borrow asked again on the next request. With no automation plugin: the same shape, naming `@objectstack/service-automation`. The gap between the third and fourth bullets is ① F.

**Dev flags and open questions (os-dev-report 6512624421).** `open_questions: []`. Deviations: (1) `Metadata-protocol: added` on the body while #27783 was unlanded, returned to `none`: the body at this head reads `none`, the changeset reads `none`, `Check Changeset` is green; answered. (2) Body opens with the seat signature line: cosmetic, no bearing. `out_of_scope_findings`: driver-odata wiring was carried into this PR by amendment 3, done; grant-bearing kinds to #26702, right (the handle has D4's shape); the 401-does-not-mark-rejected note is a correct reading of the diff and a legitimate follow-up; runtime `default-datasource-plugin` and CLI `schema-migrate` hosts without a lender refuse loudly, verified by the reason text in `borrowConnectorCredential`; #27783's stale changeset sentence is #27783's file; skills-docs follow-up is the PM's. Nothing escalated beyond the two must-fixes.

**Carried items.** `reconnect`'s refusal reworded to "when a pool is live, a failed rebuild would restore that pool" with the guard still first and the test comment matched: done. The disabled-instance flag (6511230689): visible at the lender and at the factory path, not at the OData path (① F).

**Liveness ledger.** `external.connector` flipped `planned` to `live` with two anchors and the note rewritten per should-fix (f) (static kinds resolved once and held; per dispatch only for grant-bearing kinds); `state-counts/datasource.md` regenerated 30/1 to 31/0; `Spec property liveness` green. The second anchor (the lender) is reached by the OData path; the first (`attemptConnect`) is not reached by any shipped composition until ① F is fixed, so the row's evidence should be re-read after the fix.

**Must-fix.**
1. ① F: the connect-time fail-closed refusal of `external.connector` is unreachable for a plugin-driver datasource (`already-registered` or `skipped-unsupported` return before the borrow block), so the only shipped presenter boots an undeclared or disabled instance as a connected datasource and fails every read with the cause in the server log only. Gate it in `attemptConnect` for the already-registered driver, or at the OData plugin's `start()`, and pin it with a driver adopted through a `driver.`-prefixed service; align the liveness evidence and PR body with where the gate is.
2. ③: an API key presented as a query parameter can reach a caller-facing 400 body through an upstream message that echoes the request URI; scrub the upstream message against the presented credential's spellings before building `ODataRequestError` (or refuse `paramName` for a borrowed credential), and pin it.

**Should-fix.** The lender docblock's "or the instance's declaration changing under it" overstates what a handle watches; say "after the next reconcile".
